s:
Assertion (A): MeeSeva was launched on 4 November 2011 as a single-window citizen service portal and centre network.
Reason (R): MeeSeva grew out of the APSWAN network offices of the 1990s.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is true, but MeeSeva grew out of the Naidu-era eSeva centres (2001), not APSWAN offices of the 1990s.

s: Under which Chief Minister was eSeva (2001), India's first integrated citizen service centres, launched?
x: eSeva was launched in 2001 under N. Chandrababu Naidu, not Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the principal Andhra Pradesh e-governance platforms?
A. MeeSeva
B. CARD
C. eSeva
x: CARD was introduced in 1998, eSeva in 2001 and MeeSeva in 2011. Therefore, the order is B, C, A.

s: When were village and ward secretariats launched in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Village and ward secretariats were launched on 2 October 2019.

s: When was Mana Mitra (WhatsApp Governance) of Andhra Pradesh launched?
x: Mana Mitra was launched on 30 January 2025 under minister Nara Lokesh; the G.O.Ms. No.16 e-auction portal is Konugolu.

s: With which television channel did the IT&C Department train people in the first year of MeeSeva?
x: In MeeSeva's first year, training was given through television by the IT&C Department with MANA TV.

s: What is the full form of CARD, the e-governance project of the Andhra Pradesh registration department?
o: Centralised Automation of Records and Deeds
x: CARD (1998) stands for Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department; it computerised registration.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh farmers' app won the CSI-Nihilent e-Governance award for 2017-18?
x: The D-Krishi farmers' app won the CSI-Nihilent e-Governance award (2017-18).

s: For which project did Andhra Pradesh win the Gold award at the 20th National e-Governance Conference, 2017?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Loan Charge Creation Module (CCLA)); it is added as option 5.
Andhra Pradesh's Gold at the 20th National e-Governance Conference (Jan 2017) was for the Loan Charge Creation Module of the CCLA, Vijayawada (Government Process Re-engineering). The Aadhaar-enabled PDS Gold went to Hyderabad (Telangana).

s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh introduce e-Procurement?
x: e-Procurement came in 2002, after CARD (1998) and eSeva (2001).

s: Under which minister was Mana Mitra (WhatsApp Governance) launched on 30 January 2025?
x: Mana Mitra, WhatsApp governance, was launched on 30 January 2025 under minister Nara Lokesh.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh initiative seeks to interconnect all e-governance systems through a whole-of-government approach?
x: e-Pragati interconnects departmental systems with a single window for Revenue, Registration, Transport and Municipal services, built on the Seva model.

s: What is the stated governance goal of e-Pragati in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Fully privatised delivery of citizen services
x: e-Pragati aims at faceless, paperless, cashless governance by integrating departments on a single window. It is a state platform, not privatisation, and it is the opposite of offline district-wise records; decentralised/cooperative governance is not its stated goal.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the core data hubs of e-Pragati?
x: The core e-Pragati data hubs are People Hub, Land Hub, Entity Hub, GIS Hub and IoT Hub. Finance Hub is not included in the listed core hubs.

s: e-Pragati, the whole-of-government digital platform of Andhra Pradesh, was launched under which Chief Minister?
x: e-Pragati was launched under CM N. Chandrababu Naidu during 2014-19 (APPSC 2021 key, asked twice). YSR (2004-09) and Kiran Kumar Reddy (2010-14) led undivided AP before it; Jagan Mohan Reddy's term (2019-24) came after its launch.

s: How is e-Pragati organised?
x: e-Pragati has 14 packages covering 72 projects in 33 departments.

s: Since which year has the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) of Andhra Pradesh functioned?
x: RTGS dates from 2017 and is the nodal agency for real-time monitoring, data analytics, AI and early warning.

s: Which RTGS tool of Andhra Pradesh provides disaster early warning?
x: AWARE 2.0 gives disaster early warning (used in cyclones Montha and Ditwa); AI4PGRS is grievance AI and DigiVerify issues blockchain certificates.

s: The State Data Lake at the AP State Data Centre is a single source of truth for more than how many departments?
x: The State Data Lake serves as a single source of truth for more than 40 departments and about 400 applications.

s: Which of the following concerns has been raised in relation to the Data Lake?
x: Privacy and algorithmic-bias concerns have been raised in relation to the Data Lake.

s: Mana Mitra (WhatsApp Governance) offered how many services as per SES 2025-26?
x: Mana Mitra offered 865 services (SES 2025-26), against a target of 1,000.

s: Which grievance platform of Andhra Pradesh functioned during 2019-24?
x: The order is Prajavani, Meekosam (2014-19), Spandana (2019-24) and then PGRS with AI4PGRS.

s: Which tool of Andhra Pradesh issues blockchain-based certificates?
x: AP DigiVerify holds MeeSeva and AP Seva certificates on blockchain.

s:
Arrange the grievance platforms of Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
1. Spandana
2. Meekosam
3. Prajavani
4. PGRS
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Prajavani came first, then Meekosam (2014-19), Spandana (2019-24) and now PGRS with AI4PGRS.

s: The AP IT (Electronic Service Delivery) Rules, 2011 made which of the following mandatory for departments?
x: The rules made electronic service delivery mandatory and gave legal sanctity to digitally signed certificates; they did not repeal the IT Act, 2000.

s: Which is the custodian ministry of the Information Technology Act, 2000?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
x: MeitY is the custodian of the IT Act, 2000, which was last amended in 2008 and is the parent law of the AP e-Service Rules.

s: In which year was the Information Technology Act, 2000 last amended?
x: The IT Act, 2000 was last amended in 2008.

s: In which year were the AP IT (Electronic Service Delivery) Rules framed?
x: The AP IT (Electronic Service Delivery) Rules came in 2011 and made electronic delivery of services mandatory.

s: The AP Cyber Security Operations Centre (2018) followed which policy?
x: The AP Cyber Security Policy of 2017 led to the APCSOC, set up at Vijayawada in April 2018.

s: Andhra Pradesh's IT & GCC Policy 4.0 covers which period?
x: The IT & GCC Policy 4.0 is for 2024-29, with capital subsidies, tax exemptions, employment-linked incentives and a focus on AI, cloud and cyber technology.

s: When did the AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0 (2024-29) come into force?
x: The policy came into force on 12 December 2024 with the aim of making AP a global knowledge economy hub.

s: In Andhra Pradesh's IT policy, what is a Global Capability Centre (GCC)?
o: A multinational company's own offshore unit
A public sector semiconductor testing laboratory
A third-party vendor supplying temporary clerical staff
x: A GCC is an offshore unit owned and operated by a multinational company for its own capabilities and operations, rather than a third-party vendor.

s: Up to what additional capacity does Andhra Pradesh's Data Center Policy 4.0 target during 2024-29?
x: AP targets up to 1 GW, lower than Gujarat's 7.5 GW target under its 2026-29 policy.

s: AP Drone Policy 4.0 (2024-29) targets how many direct jobs?
x: The policy targets 15,000 direct jobs (and 25,000 indirect), 100 drone companies, 50 skilling centres and 25,000 trained pilots.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Data Center Policy 4.0 – land incentives for GCCs
LIFT Policy 4.0 – up to 1 GW data-centre capacity
Data Center Policy 4.0 – up to 10 GW capacity
LIFT Policy 4.0 – land incentives for GCCs and IT infrastructure developers
x: LIFT Policy 4.0 gives land incentives for GCCs and IT infrastructure developers; the Data Center Policy 4.0 targets up to 1 GW.

s: Which department issued the AP Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-29)?
x: The policy was issued by the ITE&C Department and is implemented by the AP Innovation Society.

s: The AP Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0 targets how many startups in five years?
x: The policy targets 20,000 startups and 1 lakh jobs in five years.

s: What is the full form of LIFT in Andhra Pradesh's ITE&C policies?
x: LIFT Policy 4.0 is the Land Incentive for Tech Hubs policy, giving land to GCCs and IT infrastructure developers.

s: In which cities are co-working and neighbourhood workspaces planned under the AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0?
x: Co-working and neighbourhood workspaces are planned in Tirupati, Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.

s:
Consider the following statements about AP Drone Policy 4.0:
1. It targets 100 drone companies.
2. It targets training of 25,000 drone pilots.
3. It targets 25,000 direct jobs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Drone Policy 4.0 targets 100 drone companies and 25,000 pilots; direct jobs are 15,000 (25,000 is indirect).

s: How many jobs does the AP Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-29) target in five years?
x: The policy targets 20,000 startups and 1 lakh jobs in five years.

s: Which body implements Andhra Pradesh's Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0?
x: The AP Innovation Society (APIS), under ITE&C, is the nodal body for innovation and startups.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: OSAT – Offshore Semiconductor Assembly and Testing
LIFT – Land Incentive for Tech Hubs
x: LIFT stands for Land Incentive for Tech Hubs; GCC is Global Capability Centre, RTIH is Ratan Tata Innovation Hub and OSAT is Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test.

s: Under which programme does Amaravati Quantum Valley, India's first Quantum Valley, function?
x: Amaravati Quantum Valley works under the National Quantum Mission in quantum computing, QKD and post-quantum cryptography, with full stamp-duty and registration-fee exemption for eligible firms.

s: When is the launch of Amaravati Quantum Valley scheduled?
x: The launch of Amaravati Quantum Valley has been scheduled for January 2027.

s: Which city of Andhra Pradesh is being developed as a global AI hub, with Google's AI data centre?
x: Visakhapatnam is the global AI hub city (PYQ 2025; APPSC 2025 key), with Google's 1 GW AI data centre at Tarluvada. Amaravati is the Quantum Valley, Kakinada the green hydrogen cluster, and Tirupati an electronics cluster.

s: Where is Andhra Pradesh's Quantum Valley located?
x: Quantum Valley is at Amaravati; Data & AI City is at Visakhapatnam, the Green Hydrogen cluster at Kakinada and Drone City at Orvakal.

s: Where was the foundation stone of Google's AI data centre in Andhra Pradesh laid?
x: The foundation stone was laid on 28 April 2026 at Tarluvada, Visakhapatnam; Kopparthy is an electronics cluster.

s: For what capacity is the APCRDA data centre ecosystem at Amaravati planned?
x: APCRDA plans a 9 GW data centre ecosystem at Amaravati; 7.5 GW is Gujarat's policy figure.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: AI data-centre cluster — Adani Infra — 1,000 MW at Visakhapatnam-Anakapalli
Hyperscale cluster and GCC Park — RMZ — up to 1 GW
Data-centre ecosystem — APCRDA — 1 GW in Amaravati
Google AI hub — 1 GW — Tarluvada, Adavivaram and Rambilli
x: The APCRDA data-centre ecosystem in Amaravati has a target of 9 GW, not 1 GW. Adani Infra's 1,000 MW cluster is at Visakhapatnam-Anakapalli, RMZ's cluster is up to 1 GW, and Google's 1 GW hub (601.4 acres) is at Tarluvada, Adavivaram and Rambilli.

s: When was the foundation stone of Google's 1 GW AI data centre at Tarluvada laid?
x: The foundation of the Google AI data centre at Tarluvada was laid on 28 April 2026 on 601.4 acres.

s:
Consider the following statements about Google's AI data centre in Visakhapatnam:
1. It is the largest Google AI hub outside the United States.
2. It involves an investment of about US$15 billion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Tarluvada hub is Google's largest AI hub outside the US, worth about US$15 billion (Rs 1.35 lakh crore).

s: Which technology is a focus area of Amaravati Quantum Valley?
x: Amaravati Quantum Valley covers quantum computing, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and post-quantum cryptography.

s: Which one of the following pairs (cluster - place) is correctly matched?
x: Green hydrogen is at Kakinada; Drone City is at Orvakal, Quantum Valley at Amaravati and electronics at Tirupati.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Amaravati Drone Summit 2024?
o: Its record drone show was held at Orvakal Drone City
It included a hackathon with AP Drone Corporation
x: The record drone show was held at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, not at Orvakal; the summit itself was at Mangalagiri on 22-23 October 2024.

s: Where is Drone City, India's first dedicated drone cluster, being established?
x: Drone City is at Orvakal in Kurnool, covering 600 acres with 120 acres in Phase-I.

s: When was the Amaravati Drone Summit 2024 held?
x: The summit was held at Mangalagiri on 22-23 October 2024.

s: Over about how many acres is Drone City at Orvakal, Kurnool planned?
x: Drone City is planned over 600 acres, with 120 acres in Phase-I.

s: Where was the record drone show of the Amaravati Drone Summit 2024 held?
x: The summit was at Mangalagiri, but its record drone show was held at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada.

s: When was AP State FiberNet Ltd (APSFL), incorporated in October 2015, launched?
x: APSFL was launched on 27 December 2017; the Phase-I Network Operations Centre is at Visakhapatnam.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: The APSDWAN upgrade became operational on 1 May 2021, not on 2 October 2019. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, BharatNet Phase-II, implemented by APSFL, covers how many Gram Panchayats?
x: APSFL implements BharatNet Phase-II covering 54,502 km and 11,254 Gram Panchayats.

s: AP State FiberNet Ltd. is notable as India's first what?
x: APSFL is India's first State-owned ISP and also functions as a telecom and IPTV provider.

s: Where is the Network Operations Centre of AP Fiber Grid Phase-I located?
x: Phase-I comprises 24,000 km of fibre on an IP-MPLS ring with its Network Operations Centre at Visakhapatnam.

s:
Consider the following statements about AP Fiber Grid Phase-I:
1. It is built on a GPON network.
2. It covers about 24,000 km of optical fibre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Fiber Grid Phase-I is a 24,000 km IP-MPLS ring, not GPON.

s: Which village was the pilot fibre-grid smart village of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Mori in East Godavari was the pilot smart village of the AP Fiber Grid.

s: In which year was AP Technology Services Ltd (APTS), the nodal agency for IT procurement and cyber security, set up?
x: APTS dates from 1986, is self-financing, and is the nodal body for IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates and Aadhaar.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: APEITA — Implementation of IT and Electronics policies and investment promotion
APTS — Administration of remote sensing and GIS programmes
ITE&C Department — Parent department for IT, electronics and communications
x: APTS is responsible for IT procurement, cybersecurity, digital certificates and Aadhaar-related services. Remote sensing and GIS are associated with APSAC, not APTS.

s: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH), set up in Andhra Pradesh in August 2025, follows a hub-and-spoke model. Where is its hub?
x: RTIH (Aug 2025) has its hub at Amaravati. Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati (with Rajahmundry and Anantapuramu) are spokes, not the hub.

s: The AP Cyber Security Operations Centre (APCSOC) was set up at which place on 23 April 2018?
x: The AP Cyber Security Operations Centre was set up at Vijayawada on 23 April 2018 under the framework associated with the AP Cyber Security Policy 2017.

s: For which institution was MEDHAS, built by NIC-AP, developed?
o: Dr NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada
x: MEDHAS (Medical Education & Health Administrative System) was built for Dr NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada.

s: What kind of body is APTS, the nodal agency for IT procurement and cyber security?
x: APTS (1986) is self-financing and handles IT procurement, cyber security, digital certificates and Aadhaar.

s: Which body of Andhra Pradesh handles remote sensing, GIS and drones?
x: APSAC deals with remote sensing, GIS and drones; APTS handles IT procurement and APIS startups.

s: What electronics production target does the AP Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 (2024-29) set?
x: The policy targets production of US$50 bn and investment of US$10 bn.

s: Which one of the following is the correct target of the Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Creation of 10 lakh permanent government jobs
x: The policy targets 5 lakh first-time employment opportunities. Creation of 2 lakh first-time entrepreneurs is not its target.

s: In which year was Andhra Pradesh's Electronics Components Manufacturing Policy, aimed at building a component ecosystem, issued?
x: The 2025 policy aims at a component ecosystem, offering advance and matching incentives, interim support and plug-and-play facilities.

s: Under the Zone A/B incentive of the AP ESDM Policy, at what rate are stamp duty, transfer duty and registration fee reimbursed?
x: The ESDM Policy 2021-24 reimburses 100 per cent of stamp duty, transfer duty and registration fee; income tax is not included.

s: Which period did the AP ESDM Policy with Zone A/B incentives cover?
x: The ESDM Policy covered 2021-24 and offered 100% reimbursement of stamp duty, transfer duty and registration fee in Zones A/B.

s: What investment target does the AP Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0 (2024-29) set?
x: The policy targets US$10 billion investment, US$50 billion production and 5 lakh first-time jobs.

s: Which of the following cities host the new IT parks built in Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
x: The new IT parks built after bifurcation are located in Tirupati, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The IT Park at Madhurawada-Rushikonda is located in Visakhapatnam.

s: The Kopparthy industrial cluster is located in which district?
x: Kopparthy is in YSR Kadapa district, while Renigunta and Sri City are in Tirupati district.

s: Which is the IT/ITES SEZ of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Visakhapatnam SEZ is the IT/ITES SEZ; Sri City and Kakinada are multi-product SEZs.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sri City is a multi-product SEZ.
2. Kakinada SEZ is an IT/ITES SEZ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sri City and Kakinada are multi-product SEZs; the IT/ITES SEZ is at Visakhapatnam.

s: Where is the RMZ GCC Park in Visakhapatnam located?
x: RMZ's GCC Park is at Kapuluppada, Visakhapatnam; the IT park is at Madhurawada-Rushikonda.

s: Which of the following institutions is located in Tirupati along with the Tirupati (Renigunta) Electronics Manufacturing Cluster?
x: IIDT and a NIELIT centre are also located in Tirupati in association with the Tirupati cluster area.

s: Before bifurcation in 2014, from where did the IT exports of Andhra Pradesh mainly come?
x: Before bifurcation, Hyderabad's HITEC City and Cyberabad, developed under N. Chandrababu Naidu, generated the State's IT exports.

s: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh rebuilt its IT base mainly around which city?
x: N. Chandrababu Naidu's 1990s IT push built HITEC City; after 2014 AP rebuilt its IT base around Visakhapatnam.

s: About how many jobs were linked to IT investment in Andhra Pradesh in 2025?
x: IT investment of about Rs 1.49 lakh crore in 2025 was linked to 1,41,023 jobs.

s: What is the full form of OSAT in semiconductor policy?
x: OSAT = Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test, covered by the AP Semiconductor & Display Fab Policy 4.0.

s: Who presented the separate Agriculture and Allied Budget of Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27 (about ₹53,753 crore)?
o: Payyavula Keshav, for the first time
K. Atchannaidu, for the third time
Nara Lokesh, for the second time
K. Atchannaidu, for the first time
x: K. Atchannaidu presented the 2026-27 Agriculture & Allied Budget, for the third time. So A (Payyavula Keshav) and C (Nara Lokesh, the IT minister) name the wrong person, and D gets the count wrong: it was not his first.

s: In which year was the first separate agriculture budget presented in undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh first presented a separate agriculture budget in 2013.

s: Who is the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Agriculture Mission constituted in July 2019?
x: Under G.O.Ms.No.57 (1 July 2019), the Chief Minister chairs the AP State Agriculture Mission.

s: Who was the Vice-Chairman of the AP State Agriculture Mission (2019), a farmer and aquaculturist?
x: M.V.S. Nagi Reddy, a farmer and aquaculturist, was made Vice-Chairman of the Mission.

s: With which international institute did Andhra Pradesh partner to transform its agriculture and allied sectors?
x: AP partnered ICRISAT to transform agriculture and allied sectors.

s: Who headed the Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Commission?
x: The AP Agricultural Commission was headed by economist R. Radhakrishna.

s: How much was allotted to the Price Stabilisation Fund in Andhra Pradesh's Agriculture and Allied Budget 2026-27?
x: The 2026-27 agriculture budget gave Rs 500 crore to the Price Stabilisation Fund, Rs 14,277 crore to irrigation and Rs 13,722 crore to power subsidy.

s: Which component got the largest allocation in Andhra Pradesh's Agriculture and Allied Budget 2026-27?
x: Irrigation got Rs 14,277 crore, more than power subsidy (Rs 13,722 crore) and the Price Stabilisation Fund (Rs 500 crore).

s: What interest subvention on crop loans is provided under Vaddi Leni Runalu or Pavala Vaddi?
o: 1% up to ₹1 lakh and 4% for ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh
1% on all crop loans up to ₹3 lakh
4% up to ₹3 lakh and 1% above ₹3 lakh
4% up to ₹1 lakh and 1% for ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh
x: The scheme provides 4% interest subvention up to ₹1 lakh and 1% for the loan amount from ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh.

s: What was the annual assistance per farmer family under YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM Kisan (2019–2024)?
x: YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM Kisan gave ₹13,500 per family per year, covering owners, tenant farmers and RoFR cultivators.

s: What is the annual assistance per farmer family under Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan?
x: It provides ₹20,000 per farmer family a year: ₹14,000 from the State and ₹6,000 under PM-KISAN from the Centre.

s: What is the PM-KISAN component of Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan for landholders?
x: The scheme (from 2024-25) includes the Rs 6,000 PM-KISAN component for landholders and also covers CCRC-holding tenant farmers.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jala Yagnam — Interest subvention on crop loans
x: Panta Sanjeevani refers to the construction of farm ponds. GAP Polambadi concerns farmer field schools and Ind.GAP certification, while Jala Yagnam concerns irrigation projects.

s: Through convergence with which scheme were farm ponds dug under Panta Sanjeevani?
x: Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.

s: Which scheme in Andhra Pradesh is associated with sheep and goat units?
x: Jeeva Kranthi provides sheep and goat units, whereas Paala Velluva concerns dairy units for women.

s: Under Paala Velluva, who procures milk from women's dairy units?
x: Paala Velluva provides dairy units for women, with Amul procuring the milk.

s: Which of the following pairs regarding DBT of the free agricultural power subsidy in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: Stated target – 100% renewable energy for domestic consumers
Smart meters fitted on – Domestic connections
x: The pilot was in Srikakulam (2020) with smart meters on farm pump-sets, and the target is 100% renewable energy for agricultural pump-sets.

s: Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan assistance is paid in how many instalments a year?
x: It is paid in 3 instalments: Kharif Rs 7,000, Rabi Rs 7,000 and Summer Rs 6,000.

s:
Consider the following statements about Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan:
1. It provides Rs 20,000 per farmer family per year.
2. CCRC-holding tenants are eligible.
3. The Rabi instalment is Rs 6,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rabi instalment is Rs 7,000; Rs 6,000 is the Summer instalment.

s: From which season did Andhra Pradesh rejoin PMFBY?
x: AP rejoined PMFBY from Kharif 2022 after running Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance.

s: From which season was Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance introduced in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance started from Kharif 2019; AP rejoined PMFBY from Kharif 2022.

s: How many hours of free daytime power do farm pump-sets get in Andhra Pradesh?
x: 22.36 lakh pump sets get 9 hours of free daytime power.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Panta Sanjeevani – Sheep and goat units
x: Pasu Bhima Padhakam is livestock insurance; Jala Yagnam is irrigation, Jeeva Kranthi sheep and goat units, Panta Sanjeevani farm ponds.

s: With which of the following was Jala Yagnam (2004-09) in Andhra Pradesh associated?
x: Jala Yagnam covered 52 major and medium irrigation projects.

s: Which of the following services is NOT associated with Rythu Seva Kendras?
x: RSKs provide agricultural services such as soil testing, e-Panta, CCRC issuance, input subsidies, crop insurance, drone awareness and procurement. Issuing industrial licences is not among these services.

s: What does the term 'Polambadi' in GAP Polambadi mean?
x: Polambadi means Farmer Field Schools; GAP Polambadi teaches Good Agricultural Practices and is linked to Ind.GAP certification.

s: What is the primary objective of Soil Health Cards under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana?
x: Soil Health Cards promote judicious fertiliser use by providing information about soil conditions and nutrient requirements.

s: What is e-Crop booking at Rythu Seva Kendras?
x: e-Crop booking creates a digital crop record used as the basis for insurance, MSP procurement, input subsidy and loss assessment.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, who runs a Rythu Bazar?
x: A Rythu Bazar is run by an Estate Officer, while a regulated yard is run by a Market Committee.

s: In Rythu Bazars, prices are generally fixed at which of the following levels?
o: About 25% below wholesale prices and above local retail prices
Equal to wholesale prices and above local retail prices
Equal to local retail prices and below wholesale prices
About 25% above wholesale prices and below local retail prices
x: Rythu Bazar prices are fixed at about 25% above wholesale prices but below local retail prices.

s: With how many centres were Rythu Bharosa Kendras first set up in Andhra Pradesh in 2020?
x: Rythu Bharosa Kendras were established in 2020, and 10,778 centres were set up beside village secretariats.

s: In which year were Rythu Bazars, where farmers sell their produce directly to consumers, started in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rythu Bazars began in 1999. 1995 was when Naidu first became CM, 2004 the start of the YSR government and Jala Yagnam, and 2014 bifurcation.

s: What is the Centre:State funding pattern of ATMA, the centrally sponsored district-level extension agency?
x: ATMA runs on a 60:40 centrally sponsored pattern and prepares the Strategic Research and Extension Plan (SREP).

s: Where is the farmers' Integrated Call Centre (toll-free 155251) in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The Integrated Call Centre, set up in May 2020, is at Gannavaram, along with the RBK Channel and Studio.

s: What is the toll-free number of the farmers' Integrated Call Centre in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Integrated Call Centre's toll-free number is 155251; 1962 is the animal-husbandry app.

s: Who publishes the Telugu farm monthly 'Vyavasayam'?
x: Vyavasayam is published by ANGRAU.

s: ATMA prepares which plan for its district?
x: ATMA, a district-level autonomous body, prepares the SREP.

s: Rythu Bharosa Kendras are now known as Rythu Seva Kendras and have been rationalised to how many functional centres?
x: The 10,778 Rythu Bharosa Kendras set up earlier are now Rythu Seva Kendras, rationalised to 8,489 functional centres.

s: Which Telugu monthly is published by the Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Department?
x: Padi Pantalu is the Agriculture Department's Telugu monthly; Vyavasayam is published by ANGRAU.

s: How many Rythu Bazars are functioning in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rythu Bazars, started in 1999, number 129 functioning centres.

s: On which date were Rythu Bharosa Kendras launched in Andhra Pradesh?
x: RBKs were launched on 30 May 2020 as village-level single-window centres.

s: CCRC holders can obtain all of the following without affecting the landowner's rights, EXCEPT:
o: Permanent ownership of the leased land
Access to MSP and government schemes
x: CCRCs facilitate loans, insurance, MSP and scheme access, but they do not confer permanent ownership on tenants.

s: Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRCs) for tenant farmers in Andhra Pradesh are issued under which law, and for what validity?
o: AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011; 5 years
AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019; 11 months
AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019; 3 years
x: CCRCs are issued under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 and are valid for 11 months. The new AP Tenancy Act, 2024 is only planned; 5-year and 3-year validities are wrong.

s: Since when have Crop Cultivator Rights Cards been issued in Andhra Pradesh?
x: CCRCs under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 are issued from 2 October 2019.

s: What was the cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24, calculated as gross cropped area divided by net sown area?
x: The APSES 2024-25 recorded cropping intensity of 1.21 for 2023-24.

s: Agriculture and allied activities contributed what share of Andhra Pradesh's GVA in 2025-26?
x: Agriculture and allied activities contributed 33% of GVA in 2025-26 and support about 60% of the population.

s: According to the Agriculture Census 2015-16, what was the average operational holding in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's average holding was 0.94 ha against India's 1.08 ha.

s: Which class of operational holdings dominates, accounting for 86.21% of holdings nationally?
x: Small and marginal holdings (0-2 ha) dominate, at 86.21% nationally.

s: The net sown area of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25 was what share of its geographical area?
x: NSA was 59.14 lakh ha = 36.29% in 2024-25; 30.40% was the drought year 2023-24 and 37% is NITI Aayog's cultivated-area figure.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's cultivated area as per NITI Aayog (2020-21):
1. It was 10.1 million hectares.
2. It was about 37% of the State's geographical area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NITI Aayog reported 10.1 million hectares of cultivated area, equal to about 37% of the geographical area.

s: Which district had the largest barren land in Andhra Pradesh in 2015-16?
x: In the older land-use data (2015-16), YSR Kadapa had the largest barren land and Vizianagaram the least net sown area.

s: What is the geographical area of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's geographical area is 162.97 lakh ha; net sown area was 59.14 lakh ha (36.29%) in 2024-25.

s: Which district had the least net sown area in Andhra Pradesh in 2015-16?
x: Vizianagaram had the least net sown area, while YSR Kadapa had the largest barren land (2015-16).

s: As per the Agriculture Census 2010-11, about how many marginal holdings were there in Andhra Pradesh?
x: There were about 49.84 lakh marginal holdings, the majority of AP's farms.

s: Under Andhra Pradesh's El Nino action plan (July 2026), how many Mobile Rythu Bazaars were provided per district?
x: The plan provided one Mobile Rythu Bazaar per district, along with a control room and crop-shift advisories through Rythu Seva Kendras.

s: Among the following Kharif crops, for which was the highest MSP for 2026–27 fixed?
x: Sesamum had the highest MSP among the listed crops at ₹10,346 per quintal.

s: In 2024-25, paddy accounted for approximately what share of the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Paddy covered 20.97 lakh hectares out of the 37.51 lakh hectares under food grains, which is approximately 56%.

s: By how much did the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh increase in 2024-25?
x: The food-grain area rose by 12.85% in 2024-25, following an 11.7% rainfall surplus; 16.5% was the previous year's rainfall deficit.

s: Which crop occupies the largest area among all crops in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Paddy has the largest area of any crop in AP (PYQ 2018): 20.97 lakh ha in 2024-25, about 56% of the food-grain area. Groundnut, cotton and maize are important but cover far less.

s: Which commercial crop, called 'white gold', has expanded most in area in Andhra Pradesh in recent years?
x: Cotton ('white gold') is the commercial crop whose area expanded most (PYQ 2022). Tobacco, sugarcane and chillies are commercial crops but are not identified as the fastest-expanding.

s:
Consider the following statements about Bondalu paddy:
1. In December 2019, Kakinada farmers were advised to stop growing it.
2. Its earlier buyer State, Karnataka, had begun growing it itself.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the earlier buyer that began growing Bondalu itself was Kerala.

s: Which region is Andhra Pradesh's main rice-growing area and aquaculture hub?
x: The Godavari delta, covering East and West Godavari, is the main rice-growing area and an aquaculture hub.

s: Towards which crops is the cropping pattern of Andhra Pradesh currently shifting mainly?
x: The shift is towards fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices because of their profitability and export potential.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 11 crops targeted for productivity improvement under the 17 growth engines of Swarna Andhra @2047:
1. Sunflower and sesamum are included.
2. Sugarcane is included.
3. Redgram is included.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 11 crops include redgram, sunflower and sesamum among others; sugarcane is not in the list.

s: The agricultural and allied-sector strategy under APSES 2024-25 targets what growth over five years?
x: The strategy targets 30% growth in agriculture and allied sectors over five years, delivered through 17 growth engines.

s: Palasa in Srikakulam district is popularly associated with which horticultural product?
x: Palasa in Srikakulam is known as the “White Gold City” because of its association with cashew.

s: Which crop combination is particularly associated with the Krishna zone comprising Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam?
x: The Krishna zone grows paddy, chillies and cotton.

s: Which are the main FCV tobacco districts of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.

s: Where is the Tobacco Board of India located?
x: The Tobacco Board is located at Guntur, although Prakasam and Nellore are the main FCV tobacco districts.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Groundnut is the main crop of the scarce-rainfall district Anantapuramu. Guntur is associated with chillies, and Prakasam with FCV tobacco.

s: In 2021-22, Andhra Pradesh's rice yield was 3,392 kg/ha. What was the national average?
x: India's average was 2,798 kg/ha in 2021-22; 3,846 vs 2,844 are the 2022-23 figures.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rice yield in 2022-23 (third advance estimates)?
x: AP's rice yield was 3,846 kg/ha in 2022-23, above India's 2,844 kg/ha.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is associated mainly with groundnut?
x: Anantapuramu, in the scarce rainfall region, is the groundnut district.

s: Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts are associated with which crop?
x: Kurnool and YSR Kadapa are onion districts.

s: Guntur district is associated mainly with which crop?
x: Guntur is the chillies district and also hosts the Tobacco Board of India.

s: Which cropping-pattern change has taken place in the Godavari delta?
o: Cotton land converted to oil palm
x: Paddy lands in the Godavari delta have been converted to aquaculture.

s: Which turmeric variety is associated with the Guntur spice hub?
x: Guntur is a spice hub with chillies, Duggirala turmeric and a Spices Park.

s: Which State, the earlier buyer of Bondalu paddy, began growing it itself?
x: Kakinada farmers were advised in December 2019 to stop Bondalu paddy because the earlier buyer, Kerala, began growing it.

s: Which is now Andhra Pradesh's second cereal after paddy?
x: Maize is now AP's second cereal after paddy; older keys named jowar as the second food grain.

s: Which districts are the main oil palm areas of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Oil palm is grown mainly in East Godavari and Kakinada.

s: What was the total paddy production of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: Paddy output in 2024-25 was 127.15 lakh tonnes (kharif 78.79 + rabi 48.36); 161.86 lakh tonnes is total food grains.

s: In 2024-25, how did kharif paddy output in Andhra Pradesh compare with rabi output?
x: Kharif paddy gave 78.79 lakh tonnes against 48.36 lakh tonnes in rabi.

s: What was the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: Food-grain area rose to 37.51 lakh ha in 2024-25 from 33.24 lakh ha in 2023-24; paddy alone was 20.97 lakh ha.

s: What was the food-grain production of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: Food-grain output was 161.86 lakh t in 2024-25 on 37.51 lakh ha; paddy alone was 127.15 lakh t.

s: Under Andhra Pradesh's El Nino action plan (July 2026), farmers were advised to shift to which crops?
o: Red gram, black gram and castor
x: The El Nino plan advised a shift to red gram, black gram and castor; no compulsory shift to sugarcane.

s: Which district had the largest food-crop area in undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: In the older keyed data West Godavari had the largest food-crop area of undivided AP.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh was an Agri Export Zone for red chillies proposed?
x: Guntur is AP's spice hub; an Agri Export Zone for red chillies was proposed there.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh, the State's spice hub, has a Spices Park?
x: Guntur is the spice hub with chillies, Duggirala turmeric and a Spices Park.

s: By when does APCNF aim to cover all gram panchayats of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The target is all GPs by 2026-27; 2047 is the '100% natural farming state' goal.

s: How much ex-gratia is given to the family of a deceased fisherman in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Families of deceased fishermen receive ex-gratia assistance of ₹10 lakh. In 2024-25, ₹315 lakh was paid to 63 families.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's position in India's cultured-shrimp production?
x: Andhra Pradesh is India's largest shrimp producer, accounting for about 75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports (2025-26).

s: Where was India's first Mega Aqua Food Park operationalised?
x: The Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park at Tundurru in West Godavari was India’s first operational Mega Aqua Food Park.

s: What are the implementation period and outlay of PM-MKSSY?
x: PM-MKSSY covers FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 and has an outlay of ₹6,000 crore.

s: What is the coastline of Andhra Pradesh according to APSES 2025-26?
x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of 1,053 km according to APSES 2025-26. The older figure cited was 974 km.

s: Which country was the second-largest destination for India’s seafood exports in 2025-26?
x: China was the second-largest destination in 2025-26, with exports increasing by 20.1% by volume.

s: The marine fishing ban in Andhra Pradesh is imposed for how many days, generally from 15 April to 14 June?
x: The marine fishing ban lasts 61 days, covering the breeding season from 15 April to 14 June.

s: Under which Act was the Andhra Pradesh State Aquaculture Development Authority established?
x: APSADA operates under the APSADA Act, 2020.

s: Through which platform does APSADA license freshwater aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh?
x: APSADA licenses freshwater aquaculture through the e-Matsyakar system.

s: Which body regulates coastal aquaculture farms within 2 km of the High Tide Line?
x: Farms within 2 km of the HTL are regulated by the Coastal Aquaculture Authority under the CAA Act, 2005.

s: What is the aqua-power tariff for farms up to 10 acres inside notified aqua zones in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The tariff is ₹1.50 per unit for farms up to 10 acres inside notified aqua zones and ₹3.85 per unit for bigger farms or farms outside them.

s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's cultured-shrimp exports?
x: The later figures put AP at 75% of India's cultured-shrimp exports and 31% of India's shrimp exports.

s: Under which scheme are the 10 fishing harbours in Andhra Pradesh, with an outlay of ₹3,699.09 crore, being built?
x: The 10 fishing harbours are under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme component of PMMSY, not Sagarmala. The outlay is ₹3,699.09 crore.

s: Under PMMSY, the total subsidy is what for the general category and women/SC/ST beneficiaries respectively?
x: The subsidy is 40% for the general category and 60% for women, SC and ST beneficiaries. The GoI-GoAP shares are 24%-16% and 36%-24% respectively.

s: When was Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) launched, and with what outlay?
x: PMMSY was launched in 2020 with ₹20,050 crore (Blue Revolution). ₹7,522 crore is the FIDF corpus and ₹6,000 crore the outlay of PM-MKSSY (2023-24 to 2026-27); option D is unrelated.

s: What was the ban-period relief per fishing family from 2024-25?
x: The relief was ₹4,000 before 2019-20, ₹10,000 from 2019-20 and ₹20,000 from 2024-25.

s: What is the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA)?
o: A regulatory body under the Ministry of Agriculture
The apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce
A financial institution under the Ministry of Finance
A research body under the Ministry of Environment
x: MPEDA is the apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce for marine products. Its arms include RGCA, NETFISH and NaCSA.

s:
Consider the following statements about aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is regarded as the core of the State's Blue Economy.
2. Its markets are completely independent of foreign demand.
3. It supports over five lakh families.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP aquaculture depends on foreign markets, including the US.

s: Which of the following is NOT a stated feature of PM-MKSSY?
o: Compulsory replacement of all fishing boats with trawlers
Institutional credit for the fisheries sector
x: PM-MKSSY supports institutional credit, aquaculture insurance and supply-chain traceability. Compulsory replacement of all boats with trawlers is not a stated feature.

s: In 2017-18, inland fisheries accounted for about what share of Andhra Pradesh's fish production?
x: Inland fisheries dominate at about 82%; marine is about 18%.

s: What was the older official length of Andhra Pradesh's coastline, revised to 1,053 km in APSES 2025-26?
x: The older figure was 974 km; APSES 2025-26 gives 1,053 km.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's share of India's shrimp exports in 2024-25?
x: AP had 31% of shrimp exports; 36% is seafood export value (2018-19) and 75% cultured-shrimp exports.

s: Which of the following is an arm of MPEDA?
x: RGCA, NETFISH and NaCSA are MPEDA's arms.

s: What is the corpus of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF)?
x: FIDF corpus is Rs 7,522 crore; Rs 20,050 crore is PMMSY and Rs 6,000 crore PM-MKSSY.

s: Which pair about fishing-ban relief per family in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
x: Relief was Rs 4,000 before 2019-20, Rs 10,000 from 2019-20 and Rs 20,000 from 2024-25.

s: What is the aqua-power tariff for aqua farms outside notified aqua zones in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Farms outside notified aqua zones pay Rs 3.85/unit; farms inside the zones pay Rs 1.50/unit (the 10-acre cap was lifted in Aug 2026).

s: Where is the Andhra Pradesh Fisheries University located?
x: The AP Fisheries University (Act 2020) is at Narsapur, West Godavari.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's seafood exports:
1. Andhra Pradesh contributed about 31% of India's shrimp exports in 2024-25.
2. Exports to China fell in 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP had about 31% of India's shrimp exports in 2024-25; exports to China rose 20.1% by volume in 2025-26.

s: What were India's record seafood exports in 2025-26?
x: India's seafood exports reached a record Rs 73,890 crore in 2025-26.

s: What was the fish production of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: AP produced 55.39 lakh t of fish in 2024-25, about 29-30% of India's fish.

s: Which institution is located at Vijayawada?
x: The Veterinary Biological Research Institute (VBRI) is located at Vijayawada.

s: Which district holds the top position in Andhra Pradesh’s dairy sector?
x: Chittoor holds the top position in Andhra Pradesh’s dairy sector.

s: How is the National Animal Disease Control Programme, launched in September 2019 to eradicate FMD by 2030, funded?
x: NADCP is 100% centrally funded, was launched in September 2019 and aims to eradicate foot-and-mouth disease by 2030.

s: By how much did milk production in Andhra Pradesh decline in 2023-24?
x: Egg, meat and milk outputs all fell in 2023-24, with milk recording the largest decline of 9.41%.

s: Which of the following comparatively sustained milk production in Andhra Pradesh?
o: crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes
x: Milk production was supported by crossbred cattle and graded Murrah buffaloes.

s: India produced 239.30 MT of milk in 2023-24. What was the per capita availability?
x: India's per capita milk availability was 471 grams per day in 2023-24.

s: In which year was the 20th Livestock Census conducted?
x: The 20th Livestock Census was conducted in 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh's national rank?
x: AP ranked fourth (11.37 lakh tonnes) in meat, not first; it ranks first in eggs (2,739 crore) and seventh in milk.

s: Which allied-sector output of Andhra Pradesh retained the first national rank in each of the years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25?
x: Eggs ranked first in all three years. The egg rank is noted as having never changed.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the premium-sharing ratio under Pasu Bhima Padhakam for BPL, SC and ST beneficiaries?
x: For BPL, SC and ST beneficiaries, the Centre, State and beneficiary shares are 40:40:20.

s: What was the per capita egg availability in India in 2023-24?
x: Per capita availability was 103 eggs a year; India was 2nd in world egg production with 142.77 billion eggs.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh's 2019 Livestock Census State rank?
x: Sheep ranked second; cattle ranked fourteenth, goat eleventh and buffalo sixth.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a breed associated with Andhra Pradesh?
x: Aseel is a poultry breed, not a buffalo breed. Ongole is cattle, Godavari is buffalo and Nellore is sheep.

s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh livestock species in descending order of their population according to the 2019 Census:
A. Cattle
B. Poultry
C. Sheep
D. Buffalo
x: The descending order is poultry (1,078.63 lakh), sheep (176.27 lakh), buffalo (62.19 lakh) and cattle (46.00 lakh).

s: Up to what amount is collateral-free credit available under the relaunched Pashu Kisan Credit Card scheme?
x: The Pashu Kisan Credit Card provides up to ₹1.60 lakh without collateral at 7%. Credit up to ₹3 lakh may be available under bank norms.

s: In which year was the tie-up between the Andhra Pradesh Dairy Development Cooperative Federation and Amul made?
x: The AP Dairy Development Cooperative Federation entered into the Amul-AP tie-up in 2020.

s: What is Pashu Aadhaar?
o: A 12-digit insurance policy number for dairy farmers
A 12-digit ear-tag identification number for animals
A 10-digit bank account number for livestock credit
x: Pashu Aadhaar is a 12-digit identification number attached through an ear tag to livestock.

s: A livestock borrower under PKCC who repays within one year effectively pays what interest rate after subvention?
x: Timely repayment earns a 3% subvention on the 7% rate, resulting in an effective rate of 4%.

s: What is the unit of Andhra Pradesh's egg production figure of 2,548.74 in the 2023–24 assessment?
x: The correct unit is crore eggs; the printing of lakh eggs is an erroneous unit representation.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an activity funded by AHIDF?
x: AHIDF funds dairy and meat processing, feed plants, breed farms, waste-to-wealth projects and vaccine plants; irrigation canals are outside its stated scope.

s: Who administers the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)?
x: AHIDF is run by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD).

s: Into which programme has NADCP now been merged?
x: NADCP has been merged into the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP).

s: Which application replaced e-Gopala?
x: The 1962 app replaced e-Gopala for livestock-related services.

s: As per the White Paper on Agriculture and allied sectors (Dec 2018), what was Andhra Pradesh's rank in milk?
x: The White Paper put AP 5th in milk, 1st in poultry, 2nd in eggs and 4th in meat.

s: The Dec 2018 White Paper on Agriculture and allied sectors named which two sectors as growth engines?
x: It identified livestock and horticulture as growth engines.

s: Who launched the first-ever Credit Guarantee Scheme for the livestock sector (2023)?
x: DAHD launched it under AHIDF with a Rs 750 crore fund.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in India in meat production in 2024-25?
x: AP was 4th in meat (11.37 lakh t), 1st in eggs and 7th in milk.

s: India holds about what share of the world's buffalo population?
x: India has 59.29% of the world's buffaloes and 19.46% of its cattle.

s: How many mobile veterinary clinics (about two per Assembly constituency) are provided in Andhra Pradesh?
x: There are 340 mobile veterinary clinics, about 2 per constituency; 175 came in Phase 1 on 19 May 2022.

s: Where is the National Kamadhenu Breeding Centre of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: Under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, the National Kamadhenu Breeding Centre is at Chintaladeevi in Nellore district.

s: What is India's rank in world egg production?
x: India is 2nd in the world in egg production (142.77 billion in 2023-24).

s: When was the 21st Livestock Census conducted?
x: The 21st Livestock Census was held from November 2024 to February 2025; the 20th was in 2019.

s: Punganur, a breed associated with Andhra Pradesh, belongs to which animal?
x: Ongole and Punganur are cattle breeds; Godavari is a buffalo, Nellore a sheep and Aseel a poultry breed.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh topped milk production in September 2016?
x: Krishna topped milk production by district in September 2016 (keyed); Chittoor is now the top dairy district.

s: What is the size of the fund under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for the livestock sector?
x: DAHD launched the first-ever Credit Guarantee Scheme for livestock in 2023 under AHIDF with a Rs 750 crore fund.

s: As per the White Paper on Agriculture and allied sectors (December 2018), in which did Andhra Pradesh rank first?
x: The 2018 White Paper put AP 1st in poultry, 2nd in eggs, 4th in meat and 5th in milk.

s: In which year was the National Livestock Mission launched?
x: NLM was launched in 2014-15 and revised in 2021-22; it covers breed, feed and fodder, and insurance.

s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's fish production?
x: AP produces about 29-30% of India's fish (55.39 lakh t in 2024-25).

s: Which agency implements the Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming programme?
o: Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation
Andhra Pradesh State Agro Industries Development Corporation
x: The Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming programme is implemented by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: RySS was incorporated in October 2014; ZBNF was launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2016.

s: Andhra Pradesh launched ZBNF in 2016. What was it later renamed?
x: The programme launched as ZBNF in 2016 was renamed APCNF, meaning Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming.

s: Who developed Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF), which Andhra Pradesh adopted in 2016?
x: ZBNF was developed in the mid-1990s by Maharashtrian agriculturist Subhash Palekar (Padma Shri). Swaminathan led the Green Revolution, Kurien Operation Flood, and Fukuoka is the Japanese natural-farming pioneer, not ZBNF's founder.

s: Which award was associated with APCNF for environmental protection in 2022-23?
o: M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection
x: The M.S. Swaminathan Award for Environment Protection (2022-23) went to RySS, the agency that implements APCNF. The other awards are not linked to APCNF.

s: Besides other Indian States, in which countries is the APCNF model being replicated?
x: The APCNF model is being replicated in other Indian States as well as in Zambia and Sri Lanka.

s: In which year did the AP Community-Managed Natural Farming programme receive the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity?
x: APCNF received the (shared) Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024, announced in Lisbon on 11 July 2024.

s: Which of the following pairs regarding the Food Planet Prize 2026 is correctly matched?
x: The prize carried US$1.5 million from the Curt Bergfors Foundation and was held at Bastad, Sweden, in June 2026; APCNF was the first Indian finalist.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Jeevamrutham — seed treatment with cow dung, cow urine and lime
Mulching — sowing before rains on residual moisture
x: Ghanajeevamrutham is the solid form of Jeevamrutham. Beejamrutham is the seed treatment, while mulching is the use of crop residue or straw cover.

s:
Assertion (A): Mulching is practised under APCNF.
Reason (R): Crop-residue or straw cover conserves soil moisture and suppresses weeds.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: APCNF uses mulching precisely because the residue or straw cover conserves moisture and suppresses weeds.

s: What does a natural farming cluster generally consist of?
x: The programme works in clusters of five villages covering approximately 1,500 to 2,500 acres.

s: APCNF targets coverage of how many farmers by 2028–29?
x: APCNF covers 10.20 lakh farmers over 4.89 lakh hectares and targets 41 lakh farmers over 19 lakh hectares by 2028–29.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the action-plan coverage under the National Mission on Natural Farming?
x: The NMNF action plans cover 7.78 lakh hectares and 19.75 lakh farmers.

s: Under which system are the organic farming clusters of Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) certified?
x: PKVY is the organic farming scheme with clusters of 50 farmers / 50 acres certified under PGS-India.

s: In Zero Budget Natural Farming, what does the expression 'zero budget' mainly refer to?
o: cultivation without purchased fertilisers or pesticides
x: “Zero budget” refers to avoiding purchased fertilisers and pesticides; it does not mean that every input or labour cost is absent.

s: Which of the following is a feature of Zero Budget Natural Farming?
x: ZBNF emphasises minimum tillage, livestock integration and crop diversity, and avoids chemicals.

s: For what is Beejamrutham used in APCNF?
x: Beejamrutham is seed treatment; mulching and 365-day green cover are separate practices.

s: What is Ghanajeevamrutham in natural farming?
x: Ghanajeevamrutham is the solid form of the bio-fertiliser Jeevamrutham.

s: Which crops are used as trap crops under APCNF?
x: Marigold and castor are used as trap crops.

s: APCNF currently covers about how many farmers?
x: APCNF covers 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha; 41 lakh is the 2028-29 target.

s: Which institution has given a loan for expanding APCNF?
x: KfW, the German development bank, gave a loan; Azim Premji Foundation gives technical support grants.

s: How does the Azim Premji Foundation support APCNF?
x: Azim Premji Foundation provides technical support grants; KfW gives the loan.

s:
Consider the following statements about NMNF and PKVY:
1. NMNF promotes organic farming.
2. PKVY clusters are certified under PGS-India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: NMNF is natural farming; PKVY is organic farming certified under PGS-India.

s: Where was the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024, shared by APCNF, announced?
x: It was announced in Lisbon on 11 July 2024; Bastad hosted the Food Planet Prize 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh launched ZBNF in 2016.
2. Andhra Pradesh declared 2018 as its Year of Natural Farming.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP launched ZBNF in 2016 and declared 2018 its Year of Natural Farming.

s: By which year does Andhra Pradesh aim to become a '100% natural farming State'?
x: APCNF targets all GPs by 2026-27, 41 lakh farmers by 2028-29 and a 100% natural farming State by 2047.

s: What is the full form of PMDS, a practice under APCNF?
x: PMDS is Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing, sowing on residual moisture before the rains.

s: What kind of body is Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS)?
o: A not-for-profit company of the AP Department of Agriculture
x: RySS is a not-for-profit company of the AP Department of Agriculture, incorporated in October 2014; it implements APCNF.

s: Which scheme did Rythu Sadhikara Samstha run before it implemented APCNF?
x: RySS, incorporated in October 2014, earlier ran the Debt Redemption Scheme 2014.

s: Which foundation awards the Food Planet Prize, for which APCNF became the first Indian finalist in 2026?
x: The US$1.5 million Food Planet Prize is given by the Curt Bergfors Foundation at Bastad, Sweden.

s: Under PKVY, an organic farming cluster consists of about how many farmers?
x: PKVY clusters have 50 farmers on 50 acres, certified under PGS-India.

s: In July 2024, the ISHA Foundation honoured four APCNF natural farmers. Which of the following was NOT among their home districts?
x: The four farmers honoured by the ISHA Foundation in July 2024 came from Guntur, Krishna, West Godavari and Srikakulam districts.

s: At which place did the ISHA Foundation honour four APCNF paddy farmers in July 2024?
x: The ISHA Foundation awards were given at the traditional paddy festival at the Sripuram Golden Temple, Vellore (Tamil Nadu), on 28 July 2024.

s: Andhra Pradesh has identified how many growth-engine crops in how many horticulture clusters?
x: Andhra Pradesh has identified 11 growth-engine crops across 24 clusters.

s: Which region is known as the horticulture hub of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rayalaseema is the horticulture hub of Andhra Pradesh, with about 7.8 lakh hectares (about 45% of the area) and 52% of horticulture output.

s: India’s edible-oil import dependence declined from 63.2% in 2015–16 to what level in 2023–24?
x: Edible-oil import dependence fell to 56.25% in 2023–24 from 63.2% in 2015–16.

s: Andhra Pradesh, with horticulture GVA of Rs 1,52,950 crore, ranked third in India after which States?
x: AP ranked third after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, with 21% growth in horticulture GVA in 2024-25.

s: What is the target horticulture GVA of Andhra Pradesh by 2029-30?
x: Andhra Pradesh has set a target of ₹3 lakh crore horticulture GVA by 2029-30, covering 22 growth-engine crops.

s: Rayalaseema accounts for approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture area and output, respectively?
x: Rayalaseema is the horticulture hub, with about 45% of AP's horticulture area and 52% of its output. Option A swaps the two shares.

s: What is the crude palm oil target of the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm for 2025-26?
x: NMEO-OP (2021) targets 11.20 lakh t CPO by 2025-26; 28 lakh t is the 2029-30 target. It aims to add 6.5 lakh ha to reach 10 lakh ha.

s: What is the Centre–State funding ratio for general States under MIDH?
x: MIDH is funded 60:40 in general States, 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and 100% centrally for NHB, CDB and CIH.

s: In which year was the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), with sub-schemes NHM and HMNEH, launched?
x: MIDH is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2014-15, subsuming NHM and HMNEH. 2005-06 was the launch of the earlier NHM, 2007-08 of RKVY, and 2021-22 of NMEO-OP's era, so those are wrong.

s: Andhra Pradesh targets micro-irrigation coverage of what share of its GSA by 2030?
x: The targets are 35% of GSA by 2030, 50% by 2047, and 15 lakh hectares within five years.

s: What is the target for post-harvest units in Andhra Pradesh during 2025–26?
x: The target is 1,030 post-harvest units, including ripening chambers, cold storages, pack houses and collection centres.

s: Operation Greens, modelled on Operation Flood, covers which crops?
x: Operation Greens is the TOP scheme: tomato, onion, potato, modelled on Operation Flood. Tea/coffee/rubber are plantation crops; turmeric/chilli/pepper are spices; mango/banana/papaya are among AP's value-chain study crops, not Operation Greens.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in India in mango production?
x: AP is 2nd in mango production and 1st in oil palm productivity.

s: Which of the following is a sub-scheme of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)?
o: National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm
x: The National Horticulture Mission and the Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States are sub-schemes of MIDH.

s:
Consider the following statements about oil palm in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in oil-palm area.
2. Andhra Pradesh accounts for 48% of India's oil-palm area.
3. Andhra Pradesh also leads India in oil-palm productivity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: AP holds 48% of India's oil-palm area (2.49 lakh ha) and leads in area, production and productivity.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP):
1. It has been in operation since 2003-04.
2. Rayalaseema accounts for 71 per cent of its coverage.
3. It covers 13.49 lakh acres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: APMIP covers 37.90 lakh acres; 13.49 lakh is the number of farmers.

s: In which year was the National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP) launched?
x: The sequence is Oilseeds Technology Mission (1986), NMOOP (2014) and NMEO-OP (2021).

s: The value-chain study referred to six crops. Which one of the following was NOT among them?
x: The six crops were mango, banana, tomato, pomegranate, sweet lime and papaya. Oil palm was not included in that study.

s: In which of the following crops does Andhra Pradesh rank first in productivity?
x: AP is 1st in papaya productivity; it is 2nd in mango, sweet orange and turmeric.

s: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in fruits. What is its share?
x: AP is 1st in fruits with 15.6% of India's output.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in India in chillies in 2025-26?
x: AP ranked 2nd in chillies in 2025-26.

s: Under NMEO-OP (2021), to what level is India's oil-palm area to be raised?
x: NMEO-OP adds 6.5 lakh ha to reach 10 lakh ha.

s:
Arrange the following oil missions in chronological order:
1. NMOOP
2. Oilseeds Technology Mission
3. NMEO-OP
x: Oilseeds Technology Mission (1986), NMOOP (2014), NMEO-OP (2021).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Horticulture Mission?
o: It covers selected districts of 18 States and 5 UTs
It covers the North-Eastern and Himalayan States
Post-harvest management is one of its objectives
x: NE and Himalayan States are not under NHM; they have a separate mission (HMNEH).

s: Andhra Pradesh's horticulture GVA grew by about what in 2024-25?
x: Horticulture GVA (Rs 1,52,950 crore) grew 21% in 2024-25.

s: How much oil palm area does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP has 2.49 lakh ha of oil palm, 48% of India's area, and leads in area, production and productivity.

s: What is the fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production of oil palm in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's oil palm FFB output is 22.81 lakh MT.

s: In which of the following crops is Andhra Pradesh NOT first in productivity?
x: AP is 1st in productivity of oil palm, papaya, lime, cocoa, tomato and coconut; it is 2nd in sweet orange.

s: Under MIDH, which of the following get 100% central funding?
o: Programmes in NE and Himalayan States
x: MIDH funds NHB, CDB and CIH 100% centrally; general States share 60:40 and NE/Himalayan States 90:10.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in coffee production in India?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth in coffee production, and 100% of its coffee comes from Araku Valley.

s: Where is the ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research located?
o: Pedavegi in the West Godavari region
x: The ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is located at Pedavegi in the West Godavari region.

s: Where is the Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for vegetables in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: Kuppam hosts the Indo-Israel vegetable centre; the new vegetables and spices centre is at Gundlapalli in Nekarikallu mandal, Palnadu.

s: Sulakshana, associated with ICAR-CTRI, is a high-yielding variety of which crop?
x: Sulakshana is a high-yielding tobacco variety developed in association with the Central Tobacco Research Institute.

s: From where does Andhra Pradesh's entire coffee production come?
x: AP ranks 4th in coffee and 100% of it comes from Araku Valley.

s: Where are the semen laboratories under the National Livestock Mission in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The NLM semen laboratories are at Kurnool and Visakhapatnam.

s: Where is the ICAR-Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) located?
x: ICAR-CTRI is at Rajahmundry; the Tobacco Board of India is at Guntur.

s: Where is the headquarters of Dr YSR Horticultural University?
x: Dr YSR Horticultural University was set up in 2007 with its HQ at Venkataramannagudem, West Godavari.

s: Where is the headquarters of ICRISAT?
x: ICRISAT (1972) is headquartered at Patancheru near Hyderabad.

s: In which mandal is Gundlapalli, site of the new Centre of Excellence for vegetables and spices, located?
x: The new CoE for vegetables and spices is at Gundlapalli in Nekarikallu mandal of Palnadu district.

s: In which year was ICRISAT established?
x: ICRISAT was set up in 1972 with headquarters at Patancheru, Hyderabad; it works on dryland crops.

s: Which body supports tribal coffee growers of the Paderu-Araku hills along with ITDA?
x: Tribal growers of GI-tagged Araku coffee are aided by the Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) and ITDA.

s: In which year was Dr YSR Horticultural University established?
x: Dr YSR Horticultural University was set up in 2007 with HQ at Venkataramannagudem, West Godavari.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Andhra Pradesh has six agro-climatic zones
They are the same as the six public employment zones under Article 371-D
They include the Scarce Rainfall Zone
They include the High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
x: The Article 371-D zones are administrative zones for public employment, unrelated to the six agro-climatic zones.

s: How many agro-climatic zones did undivided Andhra Pradesh have under NARP?
x: Undivided AP had 7 zones, including North and Southern Telangana; residual AP has six.

s: In undivided Andhra Pradesh, what zone did the Krishna and Godavari areas form under NARP?
o: Part of the North Coastal zone
Part of the Scarce Rainfall zone
x: Krishna and Godavari formed a single Krishna-Godavari zone before bifurcation.

s: Which of the following was an agro-climatic zone of undivided Andhra Pradesh but is NOT a zone of present Andhra Pradesh?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
x: Undivided AP had 7 zones including North and Southern Telangana zones; residual AP has six zones without them.

s: Kurnool district belongs to which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kurnool is in the Scarce Rainfall Zone; the Southern Zone covers Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore.

s: Andhra Pradesh's agro-climatic zones continue to be listed against how many old districts?
x: The zones remain listed against the 13 old districts and were not re-cut after the April 2022 reorganisation; AP now has 28 districts.

s: The High Altitude and Tribal Areas agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh includes mainly the hill and tribal parts of which districts?
o: Chittoor, SPS Nellore and West Godavari
x: The High Altitude and Tribal Areas zone consists of the hill and tribal parts of Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and East Godavari.

s: SPS Nellore district belongs to which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Southern Zone covers Chittoor, YSR Kadapa and SPS Nellore; Nellore is not in the Krishna Zone.

s: Which districts make up the Krishna agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Krishna Zone covers Krishna, Guntur and Prakasam districts.

s: Vizianagaram district belongs to which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
x: The North Coastal Zone covers Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam districts.

s: Which districts make up the Godavari agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Godavari Zone is made up of East Godavari and West Godavari (13 old districts).

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Scarce Rainfall — Red and black soils
High Altitude and Tribal — Deltaic alluvium
North Coastal — High rainfall and laterite soils
x: High Altitude and Tribal areas are characterised by hill soils, not deltaic alluvium. Fertile deltaic alluvium is associated with the Godavari zone.

s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is chronically drought-prone?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone, covering Kurnool and Anantapuramu, is the chronically drought-prone zone of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which areas receive the highest rainfall among the agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Krishna zone and Scarce Rainfall zone
North Coastal zone and tribal highlands
Scarce Rainfall zone and Southern plains
Southern zone and Godavari delta only
x: The North Coastal zone and the tribal highlands receive the most rainfall among the zones.

s: Andhra Pradesh received 960.3 mm of rainfall in 2024-25. By how much did this exceed normal?
x: Rainfall in 2024-25 was 960.3 mm against a normal of 860.0 mm, an excess of 11.7%.

s: What is the annual rainfall range of the Scarce Rainfall Zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone gets the lowest rainfall, 500-750 mm; the High Altitude and Tribal Zone gets above 1,400 mm.

s: What is the normal annual rainfall of Andhra Pradesh, against which 960.3 mm was recorded in 2024-25?
x: Normal rainfall is 860.0 mm, so 960.3 mm was an 11.7% excess.

s: In Kharif 2026, how many districts of Andhra Pradesh were in rainfall deficit?
x: All 28 districts were in deficit; Annamayya, Prakasam, Chittoor, Markapuram and Visakhapatnam were worst hit.

s: Where was the first artificial rain (cloud seeding) experiment in Andhra Pradesh conducted?
x: The first artificial rain experiment in AP was at Atmakur in drought-prone Anantapur district.

s: Which chemicals were used in Andhra Pradesh's 2004 cloud seeding programme?
x: The 2004 cloud seeding programme in AP used silver iodide and sodium chloride to induce rain.

s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is known as the 'rice bowl' and is also an aquaculture hub?
x: The Godavari zone, characterised by fertile deltaic alluvium, is described as a rice bowl and an aquaculture hub.

s: With which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh are paddy, chillies and cotton chiefly associated?
x: The Krishna zone, consisting of deltaic and coastal plains, is associated with paddy, chillies and cotton.

s: In which cotton zone of India is Andhra Pradesh placed?
o: Eastern cotton zone with West Bengal and Odisha
Northern cotton zone with Punjab and Haryana
Western cotton zone with Gujarat and Rajasthan
Southern cotton zone with Telangana and Karnataka
x: Andhra Pradesh belongs to the Southern cotton zone along with Telangana and Karnataka.

s: Laterite soils are characteristic of which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The North Coastal Zone has high rainfall and laterite soils.

s: Where is the ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station of the North Coastal Zone located?
x: Anakapalle is the North Coastal RARS; Chintapalle serves the High Altitude and Tribal Zone.

s: Chintapalle is the Regional Agricultural Research Station of which zone?
x: Chintapalle is the RARS of the High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone.

s: Where is the Regional Agricultural Research Station of the Godavari Zone located?
x: The Godavari Zone RARS is Maruteru, not Rajahmundry.

s: Coffee and plantation crops are mainly grown in which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
x: The hill soils of the High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone (RARS Chintapalle) suit coffee and plantation crops.

s: Groundnut and dryland crops on red and black soils are typical of which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Areas Zone
x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone (Kurnool, Anantapuramu) has red and black soils and grows groundnut and dryland crops.

s: What is pre-monsoon dry sowing under natural farming, using residual soil moisture in drought-prone areas, called?
x: Pre-monsoon dry sowing is referred to as PMDS and uses residual soil moisture, particularly in drought-prone areas.

s: Which institution prepares district agricultural contingency plans?
x: District agricultural contingency plans are prepared by ICAR-CRIDA.

s: In zone-based contingency crop planning, what are agro-climatic zones mainly used for?
x: Zones decide region-specific interventions; district contingency plans are prepared by ICAR-CRIDA.

s: Which of the following agro-climatic zones of Andhra Pradesh is wrongly matched with its zonal headquarters?
x: The Godavari Zone's headquarters is at Maruteru, not Rajahmundry; the other three pairs are correct.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Scarce Rainfall Zone of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone is headquartered at Nandyal; Maruteru is the Godavari Zone HQ and Lam (Guntur) the Krishna Zone HQ.

s: Which State has ten agro-climatic zones, in contrast to Andhra Pradesh's current six-zone classification?
x: Karnataka has 10 agro-climatic zones, whereas the current Andhra Pradesh classification has six.

s: An agro-ecological zone is formed from an agro-climatic zone by superimposing which factor?
x: An agro-ecological zone is a land unit carved out of an agro-climatic zone by superimposing landform, which modifies climate and the length of the growing period.

s: Into how many agro-ecological regions and sub-regions has NBSS&LUP divided India?
x: NBSS&LUP divides India into 20 agro-ecological regions and 60 sub-regions. 15 is the number of agro-climatic zones (Planning Commission), not agro-ecological regions; '20 and 15' mixes up the two; '60 and 20' reverses the regions and sub-regions.

s: On what basis were the macro agricultural regions of Sengupta and Sdasyuk (1968) delineated?
x: Macro regions were based on climate, meso on physiography and micro on crop combinations.

s: Which institution forms the district-level tier of Andhra Pradesh's three-tier cooperative credit structure?
x: APCOB operates at the State level, DCCBs at the district level and PACS at the village level.

s: With effect from which date was the APCCADB merged into APCOB?
x: APCCADB merged into APCOB from 30 April 1994 under the Single Window Act, 1994.

s: From which year did Andhra Pradesh integrate short-term and long-term cooperative credit?
x: AP integrated the two from 1986; primary agricultural development banks were abolished in 1987.

s: Which institutions give long-term investment credit in the cooperative sector at the national level?
x: Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs) give long-term investment credit.

s: How many District Cooperative Central Banks are there in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has 13 DCCBs with 442 branches; APCOB has 18 branches.

s: As per the latest (2025-26) figures, how many PACS are there in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 2,024 PACS (2025-26), down from 2,042 in APSES 2024-25; 2,037 is the number computerised under the CSS.

s: In which year were the primary agricultural development banks abolished in Andhra Pradesh?
x: After AP integrated short- and long-term cooperative credit from 1986, the primary agricultural development banks were abolished in 1987.

s: Under which Act was the APCCADB merged into APCOB from 30 April 1994?
x: The APCCADB was merged into APCOB from 30 April 1994 under the Single Window Act, 1994.

s: Which institution refinances the DCCBs of Andhra Pradesh for long-term agricultural credit?
x: After the APCCADB merger, APCOB refinances the DCCBs for long-term credit in AP.

s: How many branches does the Andhra Pradesh State Cooperative Bank (APCOB) have?
x: APCOB, the State tier of short-term cooperative credit, has 18 branches; 13 is the number of DCCBs.

s: Under which provision of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964, is the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal constituted?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal is constituted under Section 75 of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964.

s: Which of the following is a feature of societies formed under the AP Mutually Aided Cooperative Societies Act, 1995?
o: Administered directly by the Cooperative Tribunal
x: MACS Act societies are self-reliant, have no government share capital and are run by members with minimal State control.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 97th Constitutional Amendment?
o: It added Article 19(1)(c) on the right to form cooperatives
It inserted Article 43B as a Directive Principle
It added Part IXB on cooperative societies
The Supreme Court retained Part IXB in its entirety for State cooperatives
x: The Supreme Court struck down Part IXB for State cooperatives and kept it only for multi-State societies.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about cooperative laws and policy?
o: The Cooperative Societies Act, 1912 allowed non-credit societies
The 97th Constitutional Amendment was made in 2011
The National Cooperative Policy was announced in 2011
The AP Cooperative Societies Act was enacted in 1964
x: The National Cooperative Policy came in 2002; 2011 is the year of the 97th Amendment.

s: Who heads the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Tribunal?
x: The Tribunal is chaired by a judicial officer, hears appeals under the 1964 Act and has original jurisdiction under the MACS Act, 1995.

s: Under which Act does the AP Cooperative Tribunal exercise original jurisdiction over disputes?
x: It has original jurisdiction under the MACS Act, 1995 and hears appeals under the 1964 Act.

s: Which Act started the cooperative movement in India?
x: The 1904 Act started the movement; the 1912 Act allowed non-credit societies.
