s: In its application to which of the following did the Supreme Court strike down Part IXB of the Constitution?
x: Part IXB was struck down for State cooperatives and survives only for multi-State societies.

s: Along with cooperatives, which did Jawaharlal Nehru call the other two pillars of democracy?
x: Nehru identified cooperatives, panchayats and schools as three pillars of democracy.

s: What do PACS primarily provide?
o: Crop and short-term loans with supply of farm inputs
x: PACS provide crop and short-term loans and supply inputs such as fertilisers, pesticides, seeds and cattle feed.

s: Into which of the following does NABARD support the transformation of PACS?
x: NABARD supports turning PACS into Multi-Service Centres.

s: Model bye-laws permit PACS to undertake more than how many non-credit activities?
x: Model bye-laws allow PACS to take up more than 25 non-credit activities.

s: Which of the following pairs about PACS in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
x: 2,037 PACS are being computerised; 1,490 were assigned to fertilizer companies and 1,553 completed pre-migration.

s: How many PACS of Andhra Pradesh were converted into PM Kisan Samruddhi Kendras?
x: 1,246 of the 1,490 PACS assigned to fertilizer companies became PM Kisan Samruddhi Kendras.

s: Which institution acts as the Cluster-Based Business Organisation (CBBO) for PACS formed as FPOs in Andhra Pradesh?
x: PACS in 207 blocks can get NCDC equity grants as FPOs, and APCOB acts as their CBBO.

s: India's about 8.5 lakh cooperative societies have approximately how many members?
x: India has about 8.5 lakh cooperatives with over 30 crore members.

s: How has the number of cooperative societies in Andhra Pradesh changed compared with 2001-02?
x: The number of cooperative societies in AP has decreased compared with 2001-02 (PYQ 2008); defunct labour contract and joint farming societies are being wound up. It has not increased, stayed the same or doubled.

s: How much production credit was given through PACS and DCCBs in Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: In 2024-25, PACS/DCCBs gave Rs 5,933.92 crore production credit and Rs 1,345.51 crore long-term credit.

s: Through which institutions was Rs 125.90 crore of credit given to 14,425 tenant farmers in Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: The cooperative network of PACS and DCCBs lent Rs 125.90 crore to 14,425 tenant farmers in 2024-25.

s: Political capture of cooperative boards mainly feeds which problem?
x: Boards shield politically connected defaulters, which feeds overdues.

s:
Consider the following statements about problems of cooperatives:
1. About one-third of registered PACS are inactive as per state audits.
2. Many cooperatives lack professional management and digital capacity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: about one-third of PACS are idle, and capacity gaps in management and digital skills persist.

s: Approximately what proportion of registered PACS were found inactive in recent state audits (MP and UP)?
x: State audits in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh indicated that about one-third of PACS were inactive despite registration.

s: Who chaired the Task Force on revival of cooperative credit (2004) and the Expert Committee on short-term cooperative credit structure (2013), respectively?
x: The 2004 Task Force was chaired by A. Vaidyanathan and the 2013 Expert Committee by Prakash Bakshi. Option B reverses them; B. Sivaraman's committee led to NABARD; A.D. Gorwala did not chair the 2013 committee.

s: Who headed the committee whose work led to the setting up of NABARD?
x: The B. Sivaraman committee led to NABARD.

s: In which year was the Prakash Bakshi Expert Committee on short-term cooperative credit structure set up?
x: The Bakshi Committee was in 2013; the Vaidyanathan Task Force was in 2004.

s: White Revolution 2.0 targets an increase of what percentage in milk procurement?
x: White Revolution 2.0 targets 50% more milk procurement.

s: The Ministry of Cooperation was established in which year under the vision “Sahkar se Samriddhi”?
x: The Ministry of Cooperation was set up in 2021 under the vision “Sahkar se Samriddhi”.

s: At which level does the world's largest grain storage programme in cooperatives provide storage facilities?
x: The decentralised plan builds storage at the PACS level, supported through AIF, AMI and other schemes.

s: Under the decentralised grain storage plan (Sep 2026), to what was the AMI subsidy raised from 25%?
x: The AMI subsidy rose to 33.33%, margin money was cut from 20% to 10%, and with 3% AIF subvention PACS pay about 1%.

s: What is Tribhuvan Sahakari University at IRMA, Anand, known as?
o: India's first national cooperative exports company
An urban cooperative bank development body
x: Tribhuvan Sahakari University is India's first national cooperative university; NUCFDC is the urban cooperative bank body.

s: Under the decentralised grain storage plan (Sep 2026), to what was the margin money for PACS cut from 20%?
x: Margin money fell from 20% to 10%, and the AMI subsidy rose to 33.33%.

s: By July 2026, grain-storage godowns had been completed in how many PACS of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Godowns were completed in 313 PACS with over 1.80 LMT capacity.

s: NUCFDC, set up under the Ministry of Cooperation, serves which institutions?
x: NUCFDC is the umbrella body for urban cooperative banks.

s: In which year was the grain storage plan in the cooperative sector, called the world's largest, piloted?
x: The grain storage plan with storage at PACS was piloted on 31 May 2023.
